grounds.title: Gini — относительная попарная дистанция
grounds.statement: Для n лиц с доходом yᵢ и средним μ = Σyᵢ/n > 0: G = ΣᵢΣⱼ|yᵢ−yⱼ|/(2n²μ); при нормированных весах лиц pᵢ и μ = Σpᵢyᵢ: G = ΣᵢΣⱼpᵢpⱼ|yᵢ−yⱼ|/(2μ). Безразмерен; интерпретация 0–1 предполагает неотрицательные доходы, а отрицательные могут вывести индекс за этот диапазон. Он измеряет относительную попарную дистанцию, не выбирает порог достатка или общественную цель.

grounds.title: Atkinson — явный параметр неприятия неравенства
grounds.statement: Для нормированных весов pᵢ, μ = Σpᵢyᵢ > 0 и ε ≥ 0: Aε = 1 − [Σpᵢ(yᵢ/μ)^(1−ε)]^(1/(1−ε)) при ε ≠ 1; A₁ = 1 − exp(Σpᵢ ln(yᵢ/μ)). Безразмерен. ε — выбранная степень неприятия неравенства, не параметр, извлекаемый из распределения. При ε < 1 нули допустимы; при ε ≥ 1 log/power term для нуля расходится (расширенный предел A = 1), поэтому вычислительный профиль должен объявить этот случай. Отрицательные доходы вне обычной области этого welfare-functional.

grounds.title: Theil T — декомпозиция, нулевое продолжение и профиль домена
grounds.statement: Для неотрицательных доходов yᵢ, нормированных весов лиц pᵢ ≥ 0 (Σpᵢ = 1) и μ = Σpᵢyᵢ > 0: T = Σpᵢ(yᵢ/μ) ln(yᵢ/μ), определяя 0 ln 0 := 0 по непрерывному продолжению; слагаемые при pᵢ = 0 игнорируются. Это безразмерная generalized-entropy статистика. На положительной поддержке весов при равных весах максимум равен ln n (n — число лиц в этой поддержке); при неравных положительных весах максимум ln(1/min pᵢ), где минимум берётся только по положительной поддержке, — вывод из формулы, а не утверждение источника. Canberra описывает unweighted предел ln n и аддитивное разложение within/between groups. Его операционный профиль не считает Theil для популяции с нулями или отрицательными значениями и исключает нулевые случаи; это правило профиля, а не математическая необходимость для нулей. Отрицательные значения вне домена стандартной формулы.

grounds.title: Observed association does not determine an intervention effect
grounds.statement: The observational law P(X,Y) alone need not identify P(Y|do(X)): distinct causal models can induce the same observed distribution and different intervention distributions. A causal effect is identified only relative to a declared estimand plus assumptions or a design that rule out the competing models.

source_refs.locator: Pearl (1995), abstract and article framing: diagrams combine substantive assumptions with statistical information; graphical queries address identification.
source_refs.access: Existing atlas card records Oxford publication metadata/abstract access; the full article was not accessed in this task.

source_refs.locator: Bareinboim & Pearl (2012), p. 699, Definitions 1–3: an effect is identifiable when uniquely computable across models compatible with the graph and available distributions.
source_refs.access: Official AAAI proceedings page and full paper opened; selected definitions read.

grounds.scope: This is a nonidentification result for observational data without additional restrictions. It does not say every causal query is unidentified: experiments, sufficient adjustment sets, instruments, or other justified designs can identify some queries. The data cannot by themselves verify that one proposed causal structure is the correct one.
required_inputs: A target population, treatment/intervention, outcome, time horizon, and causal contrast.
Observed joint distribution and its sampling, measurement, and missingness process.
For point identification, an explicit design or substantive restrictions that distinguish causal models; record which parts are empirically checkable and which are not.
alternatives: Randomized assignment with a well-defined treatment and adequate assignment probability.
Adjustment for a justified set of measured pre-treatment common causes under conditional exchangeability.
Instrumental-variable, front-door, difference-in-differences, or other design-specific identification assumptions when the setting supports them.
Sensitivity analysis or partial-identification bounds when no point-identifying restriction is defensible.
grounds.non_substitution: A structural causal model or DAG is one way to state causal assumptions, not a mandatory single model for every task. Potential-outcome and design-based analyses, IV or quasi-experimental designs, and bounds can be evaluated on their own assumptions. A Bayesian posterior or prior over models does not make an observationally unidentified effect identified by data alone.

counterexample.setup: Let U be Bernoulli(1/2). Model A: X=U, Y=X. Model B: X=U, Y=U.
counterexample.same_observations: Both models imply P(X=Y=0)=P(X=Y=1)=1/2, hence the same complete observed law for (X,Y).
counterexample.different_interventions: Under do(X=1), Model A gives Y=1 with probability 1; Model B gives Y=U, so P(Y=1)=1/2.
counterexample.failure: No estimator using only P(X,Y) can choose between these two intervention answers without an additional assumption or design.

task_uses: Block association, predictive fit, or a proposed graph from being reported as a causal effect without an identification argument.
Turn unidentified effects into a concrete assumption-discrimination or acquisition question.
acquisition_next: Specify the intervention and estimand before choosing a method.
Seek an assignment design, valid natural experiment, additional measured causes, or discriminating auxiliary evidence.
If competing models remain compatible, preserve their range of effects or report the effect as unidentified.

grounds.title: Adjustment identifies an average effect only under exchangeability, positivity, and consistency
grounds.statement: For binary treatment A, baseline covariates L, and a target-population ATE, the g-formula identifies E[Y(1)-Y(0)] = sum_l {E[Y|A=1,L=l] - E[Y|A=0,L=l]} P_target(L=l) if (1) consistency holds for a well-defined treatment and there is no interference (or the estimand names an allocation regime), (2) (Y(0),Y(1)) is conditionally independent of A given L, and (3) 0<P(A=a|L=l)<1 for each treatment a and every target stratum with positive mass. For a nonrepresentative sample, target-stratum weights must also be identified. When the conditional means are estimated in a selected source sample rather than the target population, target covariate weights alone are insufficient: the conditional causal responses must also transport to the target (see G2-CAU-03). The displayed sum is for discrete L; use integration for continuous L.

source_refs.locator: Hernán & Robins (2020), Chapters 3–4: potential-outcome estimands, exchangeability, positivity, consistency, and adjustment; Chapter 3.3 on target-trial protocol elements.
source_refs.access: The official author page and mutable latest-version notice were opened. Its 11.3 MB PDF exceeded the browser fetch limit; selected indexed text, not the complete book, was available in this task.

grounds.scope: These conditions give a point-identification result for the stated population ATE and treatment contrast; they are not a test that observational adjustment is valid. Exchangeability and well-defined treatment versions are substantive and generally not testable from the observed law. Empirical overlap checks can reveal support problems, but finite data cannot prove population positivity. The formula also does not identify individual effects.
required_inputs: Pre-treatment A, Y, and L measured on compatible definitions, with assignment, follow-up, sampling, and missingness information.
A justified set L sufficient to block confounding for the stated treatment-outcome contrast; variables must be measured before treatment and not selected merely for prediction.
Treatment and outcome versions, unit, time zero, follow-up, and target-population distribution P_target(L).
Evidence for treatment support in every target stratum and a plan for sampling uncertainty or missing outcomes.
For selected-source data, a defensible conditional response transport relation and source support, not merely observed target covariate weights.
alternatives: Randomization can make exchangeability plausible by design, while still requiring consistency and attention to attrition and interference.
An IV, regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences, or longitudinal g-method can use different identifying assumptions where appropriate.
Unmeasured-confounding sensitivity analysis or partial bounds can preserve uncertainty if exchangeability cannot be defended.
grounds.non_substitution: Covariate balance, a good outcome model, cross-validation, or a calibrated prediction does not establish conditional exchangeability. No particular SCM, Bayesian model, or adjustment estimator is required when a different design supplies a defensible identification route.

counterexample.setup: Let U be an unmeasured binary cause, A=U, and Y=U, with no causal arrow from A to Y.
counterexample.observation: The observed data show A=Y for every unit, so the crude treated-control difference is 1.
counterexample.causal_result: Intervening on A leaves U and Y unchanged, so the ATE is 0. Omitting U violates exchangeability; a precisely estimated difference does not repair it.

task_uses: Make confounder selection, support, treatment versions, and the target population part of the causal claim rather than hidden estimator defaults.
Separate identification assumptions from sampling error and estimator diagnostics.
acquisition_next: Collect or locate pre-treatment common causes and their measurement provenance; seek randomization or a credible quasi-experimental assignment when feasible.
Inspect target-stratum overlap and revise eligibility or estimand when support is absent.
Run sensitivity or bounds for plausible unmeasured confounding; keep exchangeability labeled as an assumption.

grounds.title: An effect transports only under explicit cross-domain invariance and support conditions
grounds.statement: A transparent sufficient transport case is: a source experiment identifies conditional means mu_a(l)=E_source[Y|do(A=a),L=l]; treatment and outcome versions are consistent across domains; outcomes have no cross-unit interference (or are defined for the specified allocation regime); E_target[Y(a)|L=l]=E_source[Y(a)|L=l] for each a on target support; and the source experiment has positive assignment probability for every target-relevant l. If the target distribution P_target(L) is observed, then E_target[Y(a)]=sum_l mu_a(l)P_target(L=l). More general selection-diagram cases can be transported by a valid transport formula, but domain labels alone supply no such license.

source_refs.locator: Bareinboim & Pearl (2012), p. 699, Definitions 1–3 and age-stratified example/formula; pp. 702–703, nontransportability witness and complete sID algorithm; p. 703 conclusion.
source_refs.access: Official AAAI proceedings page and full 7-page paper opened; selected pages 699–703 read.

grounds.scope: The standardization formula is a sufficient special case, not a universal transport recipe. In the cited framework, transportability is unique computability across all models compatible with a selection diagram and source/target distributions; the diagram's invariance and difference assumptions are substantive inputs. Data can reveal observed population differences and support gaps, but cannot alone establish that all effect-modifying mechanisms have been represented.
required_inputs: Source interventional data or a source design that identifies the conditional causal response, plus assignment probabilities.
Target data identifying the distribution of the measured transport variables L and relevant sampling frame.
Harmonized treatment, outcome, units, time, and versions across domains, with no-interference or an explicitly defined allocation-regime estimand.
A supported account of which mechanisms may differ and which conditional causal responses are invariant; source support for all target-relevant L values.
alternatives: Reweight or standardize a randomized source effect over measured target effect modifiers when conditional response invariance and overlap hold.
Use a selection diagram and a justified transport formula when source and target differ through mechanisms beyond a simple covariate distribution shift.
Run a target-site pilot or randomized study, combine multiple environments, or retain a target-specific bound when invariance is doubtful.
grounds.non_substitution: A neighboring jurisdiction, similar label, shared institution type, or source-study average is not evidence of effect invariance. Transportability need not be represented by a single fixed SCM; potential-outcome, design-based, selection-diagram, and sensitivity analyses can express different assumptions. A posterior over domains does not validate an unmeasured invariance claim.

counterexample.setup: Let C be an unmeasured effect modifier and Y(a)=a(2C-1). In the source trial C=1 for everyone; in the target C=0 for everyone.
counterexample.observed_source: The randomized source trial identifies an effect of +1.
counterexample.target_effect: The target effect is -1. Without measuring C or directly studying the target, source results and shared treatment labels do not determine the target effect.

task_uses: Re-use trial or program evidence across regions, agencies, cohorts, or time periods only with explicit transport conditions.
Expose target-population differences and unsupported strata as limits or acquisition tasks.
acquisition_next: Measure candidate effect modifiers and target distributions; retain source and target sampling and assignment metadata.
Seek target-site outcome data or a pilot intervention to challenge invariance claims.
Report the transport formula, target support, untested invariance assumptions, and any out-of-support region together.

grounds.title: When point identification fails, bounded outcomes can still yield a sharp ATE interval
grounds.statement: For binary A, observed outcome Y in [0,1], consistency, and a representative population distribution, let p=P(A=1), mu1=E[Y|A=1], and mu0=E[Y|A=0]. With no exchangeability or outcome-model restriction, the sharp ATE interval is [p*mu1 - (1-p)*mu0 - p, p*mu1 - (1-p)*mu0 + (1-p)]. The interval is identified from the observed law and the justified support bound; it need not identify the effect's sign.

source_refs.locator: Manski (1990), pp. 319–323, especially opening setup and §I on nonparametric treatment-effect bounds when mean independence or a latent-variable restriction cannot be asserted.
source_refs.access: JSTOR issue/article metadata checked; full publisher text is subscriber-restricted. Selected first-page text was available only through a nonpublisher reproduction; the full official article was not read.

source_refs.locator: Richardson et al. (2014), §2, equations (1)–(3): decomposition of the ATE, [0,1] support bounds, and sharpness under the stated minimal assumptions.
source_refs.access: The PMC author-manuscript search extract exposed the selected equations and surrounding text; direct opening hit a CAPTCHA and the official publisher PDF fetch returned 502, so the whole article was not read directly.

grounds.scope: The interval is sharp under the listed assumptions for the population mean effect; it assumes a well-defined treatment and no interference for unit-level potential outcomes, and does not identify individual effects or the effect distribution. The known [0,1] support for both potential outcomes is substantive. With unbounded outcomes, the same no-assumption argument may produce no finite bound. Sampling uncertainty, nonrepresentative samples, and missing outcomes require separate treatment. The displayed conditional-mean parameterization assumes 0<p<1 so both observed arm means are defined; degenerate-arm cases require their own missing-arm representation.
required_inputs: A binary, well-defined treatment; consistency linking the observed outcome to the received treatment; and representative or correctly weighted observed treatment/outcome data.
A defensible known range for both potential outcomes, not merely the observed sample minimum and maximum.
Treatment share p and arm-specific outcome means mu1 and mu0, with uncertainty from their estimation kept distinct from the identification interval.
alternatives: Add justified assumptions such as conditional exchangeability, monotone response, or valid instrumental-variable restrictions to narrow the identified set.
Use a sensitivity model to show how the identified set changes as an assumption is relaxed.
Make a policy choice against the whole interval using a separately declared loss, value, or ambiguity criterion.
grounds.non_substitution: A point estimate from a selected model is not the no-assumption result. A Bayesian posterior is one optional representation of added prior/model assumptions; it does not replace the support-based identified interval unless those assumptions are explicitly accepted. A wide interval is a truthful limitation, not evidence for a zero effect.

counterexample.observations: Suppose p=0.5, mu1=0.8, and mu0=0.2, so the observed mean difference is +0.6.
counterexample.identified_set: The sharp interval under only consistency and [0,1] support is [-0.2, 0.8].
counterexample.failure: The observed difference is compatible with either harm or benefit; reporting +0.6 as a causal effect silently adds an assumption.

task_uses: Represent what the evidence alone permits when confounding or selection cannot be resolved.
Distinguish an identified interval from sampling confidence intervals and from a policy decision rule.
acquisition_next: Justify the outcome support from measurement or domain constraints and collect representative treatment/outcome data.
Acquire covariates, a valid instrument, or experimental assignment only with its own identification argument; recompute the set under each added assumption.
Carry the interval to the decision layer and state whether any decision is robust across it.

grounds.title: Policy effects may depend on other units' assignments
grounds.statement: When interference is possible, a unit's potential outcome is Y_ij(z_i), a function of its group's assignment vector, rather than only its own treatment. Under partial interference (no spillovers across the declared groups), a specified two-stage randomized design, consistency, and positive probability for the assignment regimes being compared, direct, indirect, total, and overall effects of those regimes can be estimated. The estimand must name the allocation strategy or exposure mapping.

source_refs.locator: Hudgens & Halloran (2008), §1.1 on interference and partial interference; §2 on group assignment vectors and direct, indirect, total, and overall effects; two-stage randomization estimator sections.
source_refs.access: The PMC author-manuscript record surfaced selected full-text sections in search; direct opening hit a CAPTCHA. The existing atlas card reports the manuscript text was checked; this task did not independently read the whole article.

grounds.scope: The result applies to the stated partial-interference and randomized-design setup. The grouping boundary, no-cross-group-spillover claim, and any compressed exposure mapping are substantive assumptions, often not verifiable from the observed outcomes. General network interference requires richer assignment/exposure information and may remain unidentified; randomization alone does not define a policy-relevant estimand.
required_inputs: Unit and group identities, assignment vectors or a justified exposure mapping, assignment probabilities, and the allocation strategies to compare.
Outcomes measured at a common follow-up with treatment versions and unit boundaries defined.
Evidence that the design randomizes the required group and within-group assignments with positive probability.
A reasoned boundary or sensitivity analysis for cross-group and unrecorded network links.
alternatives: Use a no-interference design only where separation or evidence supports it.
Use partial-interference groups, cluster randomization, or randomized treatment saturation when within-group spillovers are the target.
Use a measured network/exposure mapping or model richer allocation vectors; if the mapping is uncertain, compare mappings or report bounds.
grounds.non_substitution: One-unit-at-a-time effects are not a substitute for the effect of a population allocation policy. No single exposure mapping or network SCM is universal; preserve plausible spillover structures, and do not treat a Bayesian network prior as evidence that spillovers are absent.

counterexample.setup: For two units, let Y1=Z2 and Y2=Z1: each outcome is caused only by the other unit's assignment.
counterexample.comparison: Changing unit 1 alone has zero effect on Y1, but changing both assignments from (0,0) to (1,1) raises the population mean outcome from 0 to 1.
counterexample.failure: A no-interference analysis misses the policy's spillover and gives a different answer from the joint allocation contrast.

task_uses: Assess policies in schools, neighborhoods, labor markets, infectious disease, or other settings where actions change peers' outcomes.
Keep direct recipient effects separate from spillovers and population-level allocation effects.
acquisition_next: Collect group/network links and assignment probabilities before choosing the exposure mapping.
Consider cluster or saturation randomization and collect outcomes under multiple allocation regimes.
Probe group boundaries and alternative mappings; where cross-group interference is unresolved, cap the claim to the supported regime.

grounds.title: Ukraine: constitutional competence and legal-method constraint
grounds.statement: Article 19(2) states in Ukrainian: “Органи державної влади та органи місцевого самоврядування, їх посадові особи зобов’язані діяти лише на підставі, в межах повноважень та у спосіб …” (21-word excerpt). It requires state and local self-government bodies and their officials to act on a legal basis, within powers, and by the manner prescribed by the Constitution and laws; Article 19(1) also bars compelling conduct not provided by law. This is a competence-and-method constraint; it does not identify the institution or provision governing a particular lever.

grounds.title: Ukraine: judicial review tests authority, purpose, evidence, rights, and participation
grounds.statement: Code of Administrative Procedure of Ukraine Article 2(2) directs administrative courts, when reviewing public-authority decisions, actions, or omissions, to test legal basis and competence, use of power for its granted purpose, consideration of material circumstances, impartiality, good faith, reasonableness, equality and non-discrimination, proportionality between adverse effects on rights and the decision's aims, participation, and timeliness. It is a review standard for disputes within the Code's jurisdiction, not an ex ante grant of power or a complete decision rule for every policy choice.

grounds.statement: Law of Ukraine No. 2297-VI on Personal Data Protection, current portal revision 2025-06-14 (Law No. 4240-IX), Article 6 requires a stated lawful purpose, transparent processing by means and methods suited to that purpose, adequate and non-excessive data, a specific lawful purpose grounded in consent or law, and retention in identifiable form no longer than necessary. grounds.title: Ukraine: open-data duty is implemented by a dated government procedure and bounded by privacy conditions
grounds.statement: Law No. 2939-VI on Access to Public Information Article 10-1 assigns information managers duties to provide, publish, and regularly update open data and authorizes the Cabinet of Ministers to define dataset lists, formats, structures, and update periods. Cabinet Resolution No. 835 (2015-10-21) implements that delegation through a specified dataset regulation and directs covered information managers to publish and update datasets. The statute's Article 10-1(3) limits open-data publication of personal data to its enumerated conditions; the publication duty therefore does not make all held personal data publishable.

grounds.title: EU: a public-task data basis must connect to a purpose-setting law
grounds.statement: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Articles 5(1)(a)-(c), 6(1)(e), and 6(3), requires lawful and transparent processing for specified, explicit, legitimate purposes with data limited to what is necessary. Public-interest or official-authority processing under Article 6(1)(e) must rest on a task or authority vested in the controller; Article 6(3) requires that basis to be laid down by Union or Member State law, determine or support the purpose, and meet a public-interest and proportionality condition. Article 99(2) sets application from 2018-05-25. This does not itself identify the member-state provision or controller's task.

Doubly robust оценка может уменьшить смещение, когда верна модель награды или модель logging policy в условиях метода, но не создаёт эмпирической поддержки для невыбранного действия.

Online FDR ограничивает ожидаемую долю false discoveries в семействе, но не вероятность ошибки каждого отдельного утверждения.

grounds.title: Within-case process evidence can warrant a bounded mechanism claim
grounds.statement: An observed event, testimony, document, or action can support a causal mechanism claim when it is an expected trace of a specified mechanism and discriminates among that claim and plausible rivals. The warrant is the trace's diagnostic force in the case and sequence, not the mere fact that the outcome occurred. Process-tracing tests differ in strength: evidence may be suggestive, necessary to retain a hypothesis, strongly supportive, or unusually discriminating; no label replaces examination of the trace and rivals.

grounds.scope: A named case, mechanism, outcome, and time interval; useful when the decision asks how an observed change, failure, or implementation pathway occurred.

grounds.non_substitution: Within-case mechanism support does not give a population frequency, average effect, or transportability claim. A source count is not independent corroboration where records share an informant, archive, author, or upstream report. Process-tracing test names do not themselves validate evidence or close a mechanism.
grounds.counterexample: In Collier's Silver Blaze example, the guard dog did not bark; this is compatible with a person known to the dog approaching, but the author treats it as a weak straw-in-the-wind clue, not confirmation that Straker abducted the horse. A similar outcome-compatible trace should not close a policy mechanism when rivals also predict it.

grounds.title: Realist synthesis supports conditional mechanism explanations across contexts
grounds.statement: A synthesis can explain why a program works, fails, or has mixed results by testing how context enables or suppresses mechanisms and produces outcomes. Its useful product is a conditional, empirically revisable explanation, often at middle range; its warrant comes from the coherence and plausibility of the evidence-backed context–mechanism–outcome account and how the account changes when contrary cases are included.

grounds.title: Comparative configurations and historical sequences support bounded, non-probability explanations
grounds.statement: Case comparison can identify whether combinations of conditions recur with an outcome and whether distinct pathways lead to it; historical sequence analysis can establish temporal ordering and trace emergence. In QCA, necessity and sufficiency are evaluated as set relations within a defined case universe. By inference from that set-theoretic definition, consistency and coverage are not population probabilities or effect sizes. A causal interpretation additionally needs credible concepts, calibration, case knowledge, counterfactual assumptions, and evidence for the proposed mechanism.

grounds.title: Lived and collective knowledge is evidence about situated meanings and consequences
grounds.statement: First-person and collective knowledge can establish how people experience a policy, what local categories mean, where delivery breaks down, which burdens or outcomes are missing from current measures, and which groups have not been heard. Its warrant depends on situated experience, elicitation conditions, inclusion and representation, interpretation, and the authority and permissions of knowledge holders. It is a distinct evidence contribution, not a degraded proxy for a population statistic.

grounds.title: Make the warrant between evidence and claim explicit
grounds.statement: A decision record should expose the claim, its grounds, the inferential warrant that connects them, the warrant's backing, the scope qualifier, and conditions that rebut or defeat it. Qualitative or historical grounds can support a bounded claim even when they do not yield a probability; their force is assessed through the relevant field's standards, source quality, and response to criticism. Explicit structure makes an inference inspectable; it does not make the warrant true.

grounds.title: Treat WG-SS as a bounded functioning measure with an explicit cut-point
grounds.statement: The Washington Group Short Set on Functioning (WG-SS) is a six-item module covering seeing, hearing, walking, cognition, self-care, and communication, designed for short census and survey use, especially disaggregating outcomes by disability status. It captures many, but not all, people with basic-activity limitations. The recommended analytic threshold is at least one domain with a lot of difficulty or inability; changing that cut-point changes both estimated prevalence and subgroup outcome gaps. WG-SS was not designed for children and is not recommended for reporting childhood disability. The guidance describes an ages-5+ fallback if the Child Functioning Module cannot be used, with expected underestimation and restricted domain coverage; it excludes children under five. One specified item asks, “Do you have difficulty walking or climbing steps?” Its question specifications support consistent translation and administration. This defines a measurement choice, not a complete account of disability.

grounds.title: Keep subjective well-being components and survey context distinct
grounds.statement: The OECD 2025 update distinguishes life evaluation, affect, and eudaimonia as separate components. Its short household-survey core module uses one measure for each: overall life satisfaction, whether one's activities feel worthwhile, and an affect item about average pain over the past seven days, generally on anchored 0–10 scales. The guidance recommends direct self-response, reports of survey mode, consistent question phrasing and response formats across modes, and placement near the start to limit priming from surrounding items. It recommends large samples for subgroup estimates (at least 2,000, ideally 5,000 or more) and phasing wording changes through parallel split samples to estimate a time-series discontinuity. These practices improve measurement comparability; they do not define a complete welfare objective.

grounds.title: Require construct-specific invariance evidence before pooled latent-score comparisons
grounds.statement: PISA 2022 provides a concrete cross-country questionnaire example: its technical report evaluates item fit across country-by-language groups and releases group-specific item parameters when international parameters misfit. For context-questionnaire items, RMSD above 0.25 triggered that treatment; a scale needed at least three items with international parameters for cross-group comparability, and reporting also required group-level internal-consistency criteria. The final RMSD distribution figures omit item-by-group cells with 150 or fewer cases because group-specific item-characteristic curves are unstable; this is not a blanket exclusion from all measurement evaluation. These are PISA-specific operating thresholds, not universal cut-offs. A comparable multi-item construct therefore needs evidence at item and group level; identical wording or a high within-group reliability statistic alone does not establish that group means share a scale.

source_refs.locator: PISA 2022 Technical Report, Chapter 19, pp. 384–386 (RMSD, parameter release, group sample-size limit, scale reporting rules).

grounds.title: Evaluate nonresponse bias for the estimate, not from a response-rate proxy
grounds.statement: FCSM's 2023 guidance treats the unit response rate as a starting point: nonresponse bias depends on whether response propensity is related to the survey item or estimate, and a rate alone omits coverage, sampling, measurement, and processing error. A bias report should identify target population, frame and coverage, design, sampled/reporting unit, mode, and key items. It should then compare relevant respondent/nonrespondent auxiliary data or use other complementary analyses, report uncertainty and contradictory evidence, and restrict conclusions where auxiliary-data coverage does not overlap the target. Analysis is estimate- and subgroup-specific; weighting cannot by itself demonstrate absence of residual bias.

grounds.title: Represent source-process changes as explicit breaks in administrative time series
grounds.statement: ONS's UK trade methods guide, revised 16 January 2026, documents a concrete comparability break: data collection for physical goods trade between Great Britain and the EU changed from the Intrastat survey to customs declarations in 2021 for exports and 2022 for imports. ONS adjusted EU import estimates for 2021–22 but says a structural break remains in the EU goods series from January 2021 and advises caution in interpretation. The example shows why a time-series discontinuity must be checked against source and collection epochs before it is treated as a change in underlying behavior. The documented case is specific to this series; it does not imply every administrative change creates a break or that every break is repairable.

source_refs.locator: Section 6, “Changes and their effects on comparability over time,” especially “Brexit structural break”; guide revised 16 January 2026.
source_refs.access: Official ONS methods webpage opened; cited section read.

grounds.scope: Repeated administrative or survey-derived statistics where collection source, frame, definitions, coding, eligibility, or processing may change over time; the ONS case is an empirical example, not a universal rule.

Time-stamped processing/revision history, source-data vintage, parallel overlap or bridge records, and revisions/backcasts for each series segment.
The target estimand and a declared decision about comparability across each source/process epoch.
alternatives: Reconstruct and backcast the full series only when common definitions and adequate historical records support that operation.
Use a parallel-overlap or bridge estimate with uncertainty when old and new sources coexist for a period.
If comparability cannot be established, retain separate segments with a break marker and limit claims to within-segment change.

Source metadata is evidence about measurement process, not itself an explanation of the causal effect.

Re-estimating within source epochs or using a defensible bridge may change that inference.

grounds.title: A fiscal amount requires a declared recording basis and consolidation perimeter
grounds.statement: GFSM 2014 describes linked fiscal statements for flows and stock positions and distinguishes accrual, commitment, due-for-payment, and cash recording. Under accrual, flows are recorded when economic value is created, transformed, exchanged, transferred, or extinguished, regardless of cash settlement; cash data remain useful for liquidity but omit noncash flows and can place an event in a different period. Consolidated GFS for a declared group eliminates matched flows and positions between units inside that group. A reported fiscal cost, balance, or exposure therefore needs its reporting unit/sector, period, recording basis, flow-versus-stock classification, and consolidation boundary stated. These choices define the fiscal statistic; they do not by themselves value social welfare.

source_refs.locator: GFSM 2014 §§3.61–3.74 (recording bases; §§3.62, 3.67, 3.69–3.73 for accrual/cash distinctions) and §§3.152–3.155 (consolidation).

PolicyOS alternative: Use accrual or a specified partial-accrual profile for event/resource timing and integrated stocks, while retaining a cash view when liquidity is decision-relevant.

grounds.title: CC BY 4.0 grants only rights the licensor can grant and requires attributable sharing
grounds.statement: CC BY 4.0 licenses only copyright and similar rights, including sui generis database rights, that apply to the use and that the licensor can license (Section 1(3), (7)). On sharing, Section 3(a) requires retaining supplied creator, copyright, license, disclaimer, and source notices where applicable, marking modifications, and linking the license. Where the grant includes database rights, Section 4 applies those conditions to all or a substantial portion of the database contents. Section 2(b)(1) leaves privacy and similar personality rights unlicensed. The grant therefore depends on the exact asset’s notice and scope.

grounds.title: EU database rights can cover substantial extraction even when database contents are unoriginal
grounds.statement: Directive 96/9/EC, in its original 1996 text, provides a sui generis right where a database maker shows substantial qualitative or quantitative investment in obtaining, verifying, or presenting contents (Article 7(1)). Article 7(2) covers extraction or re-utilization of all or a substantial part, whether or not copyright also applies. Article 7(5) addresses repeated, systematic extraction or re-utilization of insubstantial parts when those acts conflict with normal exploitation or unreasonably prejudice the maker’s legitimate interests. Article 8 preserves lawful users’ extraction or re-utilization of insubstantial parts of public databases subject to stated limits. Member-State implementation and facts govern application.

grounds.title: European statistical microdata access is a purpose-bound approval and disclosure-control route
grounds.statement: In the EUR-Lex consolidation of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 dated 2024-12-26, Article 19 permits public-use files only when a statistical unit is not identifiable, directly or indirectly, by means reasonably likely to be used. Articles 20 and 23 govern confidentiality and statistical-purpose use, and permit conditional researcher access to confidential data for scientific statistical analyses. Commission Regulation (EU) No 557/2013, Articles 3-5 and 7, sets the Eurostat route through recognised entities, proposals demonstrating need, identified data/users/facility/results, any required national authority approval, and disclosure safeguards. Eurostat’s access guidance likewise requires entity recognition and a project proposal. Approval is bounded to the permitted project and conditions.

grounds.title: Consent withdrawal and the research erasure exception have different conditions
grounds.statement: Under GDPR Article 7(3), consent may be withdrawn at any time; withdrawal does not retroactively invalidate the lawfulness of earlier consent-based processing and must be as easy as giving consent. Article 17(3)(d) is a qualified exception to erasure for public-interest archiving, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes under Article 89(1), where erasure would likely make the objectives impossible or seriously impair them. Article 89(1) requires safeguards, including minimisation and pseudonymisation, or processing that no longer permits identification where the purpose allows. A research label alone is not a retention grant or processing basis.

grounds.statement: Directive (EU) 2019/1024 excludes some documents whose access is restricted under personal-data rules (Article 1(2)(h)). Treating reuse rights and personal-data processing permission as independent checks is an operational inference from these texts, not a separate statutory formula.

Whether the reused material contains personal data or data still linkable to natural persons.
The processing actor/controller, each purpose and operation, applicable GDPR basis and any Article 9 condition.
Intended sharing, recipients, safeguards, and any restriction on the source's statistical, confidential, or protected content.
alternatives: Use an approved aggregate or genuinely anonymous release when it meets the analytical purpose.
Request a rights-cleared and privacy-reviewed release from the source body.
Process only within a valid access arrangement and publish only an output cleared for both reuse rights and disclosure rules.
grounds.non_substitution: A licence answers only the rights it grants; it cannot establish the controller's GDPR basis or override an access restriction. Conversely, a lawful processing basis does not establish a copyright or database-right grant for public redistribution.
grounds.counterexample: Hypothetical counterexample (PolicyOS inference): a public catalogue offers a CC-licensed table with identifiable benefit or health records. The licence does not itself resolve personal-data access and processing permission.
grounds.task_uses: PolicyOS inference: track rights clearance separately from processing permission at acquisition and export; identify the licensor/access authority separately from the controller and purpose.
grounds.acquisition_next: Operational route (inference): resolve the exact document and licence with its holder, then separately obtain the controller’s basis, purpose, and any special-category condition. If either remains unresolved, seek an approved aggregate or declare the limitation.

grounds.title: Metrological traceability relates a result to a reference; it does not certify truth or fitness
grounds.statement: Source-established: VIM 2.41 treats traceability as a documented calibration chain from result to reference, with each link contributing to uncertainty; it requires the reference time and says traceability alone does not establish purpose-adequate uncertainty or absence of mistakes. PolicyOS application (inference): keep reference-chain support distinct from construct validity, result accuracy, and downstream fitness. A multi-input measurement model may require branched chains.

source_refs.locator: VIM 3, entries 2.40 and 2.41, notes 2–5: calibration hierarchy, time of reference, branched inputs, and express non-guarantee of fitness/error absence
source_refs.access: Official BIPM PDF opened; selected entries 2.40–2.41 read directly.

source_refs.locator: ILAC P10:07/2020, §§1–2: chain definition, suitable reference and calibration routes
source_refs.access: Official ILAC PDF opened; selected clauses read directly.

grounds.scope: Physical quantities measured by instruments, standards, or reference materials for which a calibration hierarchy can be defined. This does not settle whether an operationalized physical quantity validly represents a non-physical policy construct.
required_inputs: Claim-specific measurand, unit or non-SI reference, relevant range, location/population, and intended decision.
Exact measurement system/instrument identity, procedure and version, calibration certificates, reference identity and reference-use time for each link, and the uncertainty contributed at each link.
All material input quantities in the measurement model, including branch-specific calibration records and relative contribution to the result; measurement/environment conditions and any corrections.

For an asserted recognized route, the calibration provider's service/range and scope as of the calibration date; for other routes, the documented basis establishing a suitable reference and competent procedure.
alternatives: Trace to a practical realization of an SI unit through a suitable NMI service or an accredited laboratory whose scope covers the calibration.

Where SI traceability is inappropriate or technically unavailable, use an appropriate certified reference material or a clearly defined non-SI reference/procedure with documented comparison and task-specific suitability evidence, following the bounded alternatives ILAC P10 describes.
If no reference relation is established, retain the result with an explicit unresolved-reference limitation; do not infer either zero error or no measurement.
grounds.non_substitution: A certificate, accreditation logo, calibration date, or unbroken reference chain is not a verdict that the observation is correct, the chosen measurand represents the intended construct, the uncertainty resolves the decision boundary, or the result is causal evidence.
grounds.counterexample: A sensor certificate contains a complete chain to SI, but its calibrated range omits the policy threshold or its uncertainty is wider than the distance between the observed value and that threshold. The chain can be traceable while the result remains unable to support the proposed threshold decision.
task_uses: Separate reference-chain integrity from measurement fitness and substantive claim support.
Acquire calibration evidence for the exact instrument, range, procedure, and time used by the claim rather than relying on a generic lab or source badge.
grounds.acquisition_next: For a concrete measurement, retrieve the original calibration certificate and contemporaneous service scope; resolve each reference and calibration date, the instrument range, uncertainty contributors, environment, and any adjustment or as-found/as-left record. Check the corresponding BIPM KCDB CMC or accreditation-body scope where that route is claimed. If SI is not the right reference, identify a suitable reference procedure/CRM and obtain its certificate and use conditions.

grounds.title: Measurement uncertainty characterizes a result; it does not choose tolerance or fitness for action
grounds.statement: Source-established: GUM §§1.1–1.4 gives general rules for uncertainty of a defined measurand and expressly leaves tolerance-setting and safe-action use to application-specific rules. PolicyOS application (inference): report measurement uncertainty separately from tolerance/fitness, and do not import GUM to survey, causal, forecast, or value uncertainty without a suitable method.

source_refs.locator: JCGM 100:2008(E), §§1.1–1.4; §1.4 names tolerance and safe-action decisions as uses the guide itself does not prescribe
source_refs.access: Official BIPM PDF opened; §§1.1–1.4 read directly.

source_refs.locator: VIM 3, entry 2.41 note 5: traceability does not establish purpose-adequate uncertainty
source_refs.access: Official BIPM PDF opened; entry 2.41 and notes read directly.

grounds.scope: Quantitative physical measurement uncertainty evaluated against a defined measurement model. A survey estimate, causal-effect interval, forecast range, or value disagreement needs its own uncertainty model and cannot inherit this guide merely because it is reported numerically.
required_inputs: Measurand, measurement procedure/model, scope and intended use, including relevant time and environmental conditions.

Input estimates, uncertainty components and distributions, covariance where relevant, evaluation method, corrections, assumptions, and the reported standard or expanded uncertainty with its coverage factor/probability interpretation.
A separately sourced tolerance/requirement or action purpose, plus the rule that maps a measured result and its uncertainty to an outcome.
alternatives: Use a domain-specific uncertainty/evaluation method where the construct, measurement process, or regulatory application needs detail beyond the general GUM rules; pin its version and the exact measured property.
For measurements represented by a distribution or dependent on time/parameters, define the additional measurands and describe the dependence instead of compressing it into one scalar interval.

Where the phenomenon or data-generating design does not support a GUM-style measurement uncertainty, report the appropriate sampling, model, or qualitative limitation rather than relabeling it as metrological uncertainty.
grounds.non_substitution: An uncertainty budget cannot supply an authorized tolerance or decide who should bear false-acceptance versus false-rejection risk. A small uncertainty does not establish that the measured quantity is the policy-relevant construct; a large one does not by itself establish that the measurement is useless for every task.
grounds.counterexample: The same thermometer result and uncertainty may be adequate for estimating a broad seasonal trend yet too imprecise to decide whether one facility crossed an enforcement threshold. The result's uncertainty is unchanged; the tolerance, cost of wrong decisions, and fitness question differ.
task_uses: Keep result characterization, requirements, and action fitness as separate evidence relations.
Make interval interpretation and uncertainty-model assumptions visible before calculating a pass/fail or safety conclusion.
grounds.acquisition_next: Acquire the full measurement model and component budget for the actual procedure, not just the printed ± value. Separately acquire the governing tolerance and who set it. Because the BIPM publication list checked on 2026-10-21 also lists JCGM 100:2008/Amd.1:2026 on nonlinear models, check that amendment's text before relying on the base GUM for a nonlinear model; its text was not reviewed in this wave.

grounds.title: Measurement-based conformity is requirement plus decision rule, with explicit error trade-offs
grounds.statement: Source-established: JCGM 106 defines a decision rule as the documented use of uncertainty when accepting or rejecting against a requirement; simple acceptance and guard bands yield different consumer/producer error trade-offs. PolicyOS application (inference): neither the measurement nor JCGM 106 chooses the operative requirement or acceptable public-policy risk, so preserve the governing decision and conditional outcomes separately.

source_refs.locator: JCGM 106:2012, §3.3.12 (decision rule), §7 (conformance probability), §§8.2–8.3 (simple acceptance, shared risk, and guard bands), §9 (consumer/producer risks); §8.3.3, Example 1 (speed-limit enforcement) illustrates a purpose-specific confidence threshold
source_refs.access: Official BIPM PDF opened; selected clauses and example read directly.

source_refs.access: Official BIPM PDF opened; selected clause read directly.

grounds.scope: Conformity decisions where a specified item/property is measured against a stated requirement and the measurement uncertainty can be characterized. The guide's equations/examples do not automatically transfer to a policy design, non-measurement criterion, or jurisdiction without a separate governing rule.
required_inputs: The requirement itself, its issuer/authority, scope, effective period, exact property, units, tolerance limits, and the protected action the result controls.
Measured value and uncertainty distribution/coverage appropriate to the measurand, method, range, and relevant measurement conditions.
A documented decision rule chosen before interpreting the result, the acceptance/rejection/indeterminate zones, and the stated treatment of consumer and producer consequences or other error costs.
The authority or parties responsible for choosing the requirement and risk trade-off; analytical guidance alone cannot fill that role.
alternatives: Use simple acceptance/shared-risk when its shared error exposure is explicitly acceptable under the governing rule.

Use guarded acceptance or guarded rejection when reducing a specified false-acceptance or false-rejection risk justifies the corresponding cost; calculate the guard band under the stated distributional assumptions.
Use an indeterminate/retest/referral band when the result is too close to the limit for the chosen rule to support a binary decision, if the governing process permits it.
grounds.non_substitution: A numeric limit does not specify the decision rule; a decision rule does not authorize the underlying limit. A conformity result under one rule is not a general verified badge, nor does it establish causal effect or overall policy acceptability.
grounds.counterexample: PolicyOS-created illustration (not a source result or recommended rule): with an upper limit of 100 and a result of 99 ±2, simple acceptance can accept the point result while a predeclared guarded-acceptance rule requiring result plus expanded uncertainty to stay below 100 will not establish conformity. The result is identical; the separately chosen rule changes its decision use.
task_uses: Expose the source and version of a conformity requirement separately from the measurement and uncertainty.
Show why a result is admitted, limited, retested, rejected, or indeterminate under the actual decision rule and its risk assumptions.
grounds.acquisition_next: For a real decision, obtain the operative requirement and decision rule from the competent source, confirm when it applied, then bind the measurement distribution and method to the rule. If the governing institution has not set a rule or risk allocation, retain alternative conditional outcomes rather than selecting one silently.

grounds.title: Accreditation is evidence about a scoped service route, not a universal pass for every result
grounds.statement: Source-established: ILAC P10’s recognized traceability routes require a service suitable for the intended use and a matching scope; Appendix A identifies technical-competence and traceability evidence for less-recognized routes. PolicyOS application (inference): accreditation is a scoped service signal; the claim-specific checklist below is an evidence demand, not a source-prescribed universal test. Verify the calibration date/range/scope and still evaluate task fitness.

source_refs.locator: ILAC P10:07/2020, §2 routes 1–3b and notes 1–4 (PDF pp. 6–8); Appendix A evidence list and practical-assessment guidance (PDF pp. 10–11)
source_refs.access: Official ILAC PDF opened; selected clauses read directly.

grounds.scope: Testing, calibration, and other conformity-assessment activities involving measurement within the ILAC policy framework; P10 also addresses in-house calibration and certified reference materials. Use outside this framework requires its own authority and competence basis.
required_inputs: Original calibration certificate plus provider, instrument, measurand/range, method, calibration date, and stated uncertainty.
A dated KCDB CMC or accreditation-body record showing that the exact service/range was covered at calibration time.
For a non-ordinary route: independently reviewable method, uncertainty, result-validity, personnel, equipment, facility/environment, and audit evidence; identify who assessed it.
The task-specific tolerance or decision purpose needed to judge whether the service uncertainty and range are adequate.
alternatives: Use an NMI service whose contemporaneous KCDB CMC covers the calibration range.
Use an accredited-laboratory service shown in the accreditation body’s dated scope.

When ordinary routes are unavailable, require competent independent review of a fallback route; if SI is unavailable or inapplicable, use a suitable CRM or documented comparison to an accepted reference procedure, method, or consensus standard.
grounds.non_substitution: The accreditation mark establishes neither that every service of the laboratory is in scope nor that the chosen calibration is adequate for the task. A calibration provider's competence cannot establish the semantic validity of a construct or the truth of a downstream claim.
grounds.counterexample: A calibration certificate carries a recognized accreditation mark, but its listed scope covers another quantity or range. A consumer who checks only the issuer/logo would report an assurance pass even though the particular service is outside the scope the ILAC route requires.
task_uses: Check measurement assurance evidence at the service-and-range level instead of promoting a provider-level badge.
Name the evidence deficit and a feasible fallback assessment when recognized scope is absent, rather than treating absence of accreditation as proof of invalidity or as a free pass.
grounds.acquisition_next: Resolve the provider's exact scope and status from the responsible accreditation body or BIPM KCDB for the calibration date; retrieve the result certificate and the stated uncertainty. If using an exception route, request the Appendix A records from the provider and arrange an independent competent review. Keep the ISO texts referenced by ILAC as a separate acquisition step if a task needs their normative clauses; they were not accessed in this review.

grounds.title: Provenance and revocation are typed change evidence; each dependent claim needs scoped reassessment
grounds.statement: Source-established: W3C VC v2 supports tamper-evident issuer claims and status signals such as suspension or revocation; it leaves issuer trust and purpose-specific claim validation to the verifier, and warns that a valid signature/status does not make every credential valid for every context. PolicyOS application (inference): treat a verified status change as a trigger to revisit dependent uses, not a blanket truth verdict; preserve the earlier decision and its time basis.

source_refs.locator: W3C VC Data Model v2.0 (Recommendation 2025-05-15), §§4.10, 5.1, 9.9.2, and Appendix A.6–A.10: credential status, verifier-specific issuer trust, claim validation, and fitness-for-purpose checks

grounds.scope: Signed credentials or institutional attestations whose current validity or use as evidence depends on a declared issuer/status scheme. It does not prescribe a status scheme for calibration certificates, academic publications, or other resources.
required_inputs: Exact credential/version and subject/claim; issuer identity and applicable signing proof/key status.
Declared credentialStatus type and status source, the actual status response/event, retrieval/receipt time, any issuer-supplied effective time or reason, and verification cutoff.
The verifier’s purpose-specific issuer-trust and claim-validation rule, including which claim must be current for the decision.
A supported dependency relation from the credential claim to each affected result/publication and any independent basis that may preserve it.
alternatives: Query the issuer’s declared status mechanism/register and verify the result against the exact credential and status type; acquire an updated credential where the issuer’s process requires reissue.
If no valid status mechanism or authoritative response is available, report current status as unresolved at the stated cutoff and limit any use that requires present validity.

For other source types (e.g. a paper correction or calibration scope change), seek that source type’s responsible publisher, repository, NMI, or accreditation-body record rather than treating VC status as a universal revocation feed.
grounds.non_substitution: A valid proof binds an issuer to particular signed bytes, and a status mechanism reports credential status under its scheme. Neither proves that the issuer is competent for this purpose, the claim is substantively true, the status feed is complete, or a downstream claim is materially affected.
grounds.counterexample: PolicyOS-created illustration: revocation of a professional-license credential can remove its current-status warrant for a decision requiring a present license while leaving intact the historical fact that the credential was once issued. Whether a dependent decision changes depends on its purpose, status event, and effective time.
task_uses: Separate content integrity, issuer identity/trust, present credential status, and truth/fitness of the underlying claim.
Revisit uses whose dependency and purpose actually require the changed status; preserve the earlier claim state and its time cutoff for replay.
Expose missing status mechanisms and unresolved event scope instead of treating signature validity or last fetch as current truth.
grounds.acquisition_next: For an actual credential-backed claim, resolve the credential and status scheme, query the issuer’s status source through an authorized/privacy-safe route, record the response cutoff and event scope, and reconstruct which claims require that credential to be current. If status is unavailable or the verifier’s purpose/trust rule is absent, leave current validity not established and ask the responsible claim/currentness owner to determine the scoped reaction.

grounds.title: EU institutional authority must be traced to conferred and instrument-specific powers
grounds.statement: TEU Article 5 confines Union action to Treaty-conferred competences; Article 13(2) confines each institution to Treaty-conferred powers and their procedures, conditions and objectives. TFEU Articles 290–291 distinguish delegated amendment or supplementation of non-essential elements from implementing powers conferred where uniform implementation conditions are needed. PolicyOS inference: these distinctions support a candidate-level trace from actor and action to a specific Treaty basis and, where used, the parent act’s delegation or implementing-power clause. They do not themselves adjudicate a concrete act’s legality.

grounds.scope: EU institutional action under the TEU and TFEU, including delegated and implementing acts. A concrete legal opinion, domestic competence finding, or review of a named act is outside this research ground.
required_inputs: Identified institution or other actor, proposed act, target and relevant time.
The precise Treaty legal basis and required procedure, conditions and objectives.
For a delegated or implementing measure, the parent legislative act and its scope, duration, conditions, scrutiny and current version.
The final instrument and its official publication or notification record.
alternatives: The relevant power may remain with Member States if not conferred on the Union.
A direct Treaty power, legislative procedure, delegated power and implementing power are distinct routes and must be resolved from the actual instrument.
An institution may issue non-binding communications that do not themselves exercise the power asserted for a later binding act.
grounds.non_substitution: An institution’s mission statement, policy priority, organizational chart, signature or prior activity does not establish the Treaty basis or procedure for this act. A cited legal basis also does not prove the act fits that basis.
grounds.counterexample: A Commission policy statement supports action on public health, but a later delegated act that changes an essential element cannot be justified by the statement: Article 290 reserves essential elements to the legislative act and requires an express parent-act delegation.

grounds.title: An EU budget appropriation and a basic act establish different parts of spending authority
grounds.statement: TFEU Articles 310 and 314 provide for annual expenditure authorization and an annual budget established by Parliament and Council. Article 310(3) requires a prior legally binding Union act for implementation of budget expenditure, subject to the financial rules. Financial Regulation 2024/2509 Article 58 generally requires a basic act before appropriations for Union action are used, while listing conditional exceptions. The 2026 Definitive Adoption is a concrete annual budget act. PolicyOS inference: that act alone does not identify the applicable basic act, recipient eligibility, commitment, or payment.

grounds.scope: EU annual budget expenditure and the legal instruments needed to implement it. This does not resolve national budgets, a particular programme’s eligibility, or a named authorising officer’s powers.
required_inputs: Financial year and the original budget line plus any relevant amending budget or transfer.
Commitment versus payment appropriation and the applicable basic act or a specifically supported Financial Regulation exception.
Programme conditions, responsible authorising actor, legal or budgetary commitment, and payment evidence if execution is claimed.
alternatives: A different year, line, amending budget, transfer, or funding instrument may govern.
Financial Regulation Article 58(2)–(5) provides limited, conditioned exceptions; the proposed action must still fall within Union competence.
A budget appropriation can be available while a programme’s implementing act, eligibility decision, or commitment remains absent.
grounds.non_substitution: A budget heading or announced allocation does not establish substantive competence, an adopted basic act, eligibility, a legal commitment, payment, or delivery capacity. Conversely, a basic act does not prove that funds were appropriated or spent.

grounds.title: EU entry into force depends on the act class and its publication or notification path
grounds.statement: TFEU Article 297 sets different formal paths: legislative acts and specified generally addressed non-legislative acts are published in the Official Journal and take effect on their stated date or, absent one, the twentieth day after publication; other directives and decisions addressed to identified recipients take effect on notification. PolicyOS inference: a vote, adoption announcement, signature, or OJ page alone may not settle the applicable date without the act class, clause and notification record. Entry into force and a separately stated application date should be represented separately.

source_refs.access: Official EUR-Lex selected article text; clauses only.

grounds.scope: EU legal acts covered by Article 297. It is a date-resolution rule, not a determination that a named act was validly adopted or correctly classified.
required_inputs: Final signed act and its legal form and addressees.
The relevant OJ edition and publication date or recipient-specific notification evidence.
The act’s entry-into-force, application, transitional, amendment and repeal clauses.
alternatives: An act may specify a different entry-into-force date.
An addressee-specific directive or decision follows notification rather than the general publication default in Article 297(2).
A later application date may follow entry into force.
grounds.non_substitution: Parliamentary or committee adoption records, institutional announcements, signatures, and consolidated-text timestamps are not interchangeable with the act-specific publication or notification event that governs its effect.

grounds.title: Ukraine separates parliamentary adoption, presidential promulgation and a law’s effective date
grounds.statement: Constitution of Ukraine Article 94 requires the Speaker to sign and forward an adopted law. Within 15 days after receipt, the President must sign and officially promulgate it or return reasoned proposals; failure to return it within that period means it is deemed approved and must be signed and promulgated. After two-thirds re-adoption, the President must sign and promulgate within ten days; if the President does not sign, the Speaker promulgates and publishes it with the Speaker’s signature. A law takes effect ten days after official promulgation unless it sets another date, which cannot precede publication.

source_refs.locator: Article 94, paragraphs 1–5, including non-return and Speaker promulgation branches; official portal states current revision 2020-01-01

grounds.scope: Ukraine’s constitutional law-making and promulgation sequence for ordinary laws under Article 94. Other act classes, constitutional amendments, special commencement rules and later legal interpretation may differ.
required_inputs: Final law identifier and adoption record, distinct from draft or bill status.
Speaker signature/forwarding event and presidential signature, return, veto-override or deemed-approval path.
Official promulgation/publication record plus the law’s own commencement clause and version applicable at the relevant time.
alternatives: The law may set its own entry-into-force date, subject to the constitutional publication floor.
A veto and two-thirds re-adoption use the special path in Article 94.
A different Ukrainian instrument class may follow a different constitutional or statutory procedure.
grounds.non_substitution: A parliamentary vote or bill page does not by itself establish completed promulgation or the date the law became effective. A translated summary also does not replace the operative Ukrainian text and its official publication record.
grounds.counterexample: Hypothetical PolicyOS example: the task has a parliamentary-vote record but no verified promulgation or publication record. That narrow evidence does not establish completion of the Article 94 sequence; neither does an absent display entry prove that the institutional event never occurred. Obtain the law text and the relevant official event records before determining effective status.
